source: CIC-IDS2017 MachineLearningCSV (no IP addresses or timestamps in these files)

DoS.title: Denial of Service
DoS.description: One host floods a service (HTTP floods, Slowloris, slow-POST) to exhaust it.
actions: Rate-limit or temporarily block the source at the edge firewall / load balancer.
Check the target service for exhausted worker pools or connection tables.
Enable slow-request timeouts (e.g. reverse-proxy header/body timeouts).

DDoS.title: Distributed Denial of Service
DDoS.description: Many sources flood a target at once, saturating bandwidth or the service.
actions: Engage upstream DDoS scrubbing / CDN protection for the targeted address.
Apply geo or ASN rate limits; block the top offending source ranges.
Watch service health and bandwidth on the targeted link.

PortScan.title: Port Scan / Reconnaissance
PortScan.description: A host probes many ports to map running services, usually before an attack.
actions: Block or tarpit the scanning source; check whether it is an internal host.
Review which ports answered and close services that should not be exposed.
Raise monitoring on the scanned hosts: an attack often follows a scan.

BruteForce.title: Credential Brute Force
BruteForce.description: Repeated login attempts against FTP/SSH or similar services.
actions: Lock or throttle the targeted accounts; block the source IP.
Check authentication logs for any successful login from the source.
Enforce MFA and key-based SSH; disable password login where possible.

WebAttack.title: Web Application Attack
WebAttack.description: SQL injection, XSS or login brute force against a web application.
actions: Inspect the web server / WAF logs for the payloads sent by the source.
Block the source and enable WAF rules for SQLi / XSS.
Check the application database for unexpected changes or data access.

Bot.title: Botnet / Command and Control
Bot.description: An infected host beacons to a controller for commands (e.g. Ares botnet).
actions: Isolate the internal host: it is likely already compromised.
Block the controller address/domain at the firewall and DNS.
Run endpoint forensics on the host and look for the same beacon elsewhere.

Infiltration.title: Network Infiltration
Infiltration.description: A host inside the network, compromised via a malicious file, attacks or scans from within.
actions: Isolate the internal host immediately and preserve it for forensics.
Find how the payload arrived (email, download) and block that path.
Hunt for the same behaviour on other hosts; reset credentials used on the host.

Heartbleed.title: Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160)
Heartbleed.description: Malformed TLS heartbeats leak server memory, including keys and passwords.
actions: Patch OpenSSL on the target immediately.
Revoke and reissue TLS certificates/keys; force password resets.
Assume memory contents leaked: review what the server held.

Novel.title: Unknown anomalous behaviour
Novel.description: Traffic that the anomaly models find highly unusual but that does not match any known attack family. Could be a new (zero-day) attack, a misconfiguration or rare legitimate traffic.
actions: Review the top deviating features listed in the explanation.
Check whether the source/destination is expected to talk this way.
If benign, mark it as a false positive so it can be learned as normal.

anomaly.thresholds: quantile (1 - target_fpr) of calibration-slice benign scores

insights: 347 alerts are novel (no known attack signature matched). Review them first for zero-day activity, then mark confirmed false positives so the baseline can learn them.
Unknown anomalous behaviour: one source touched 77 ports; treat it as reconnaissance and expect follow-up attacks on the open ones.

incidents.title: Credential Brute Force

actions: Lock or throttle the targeted accounts; block the source IP.

incidents.title: Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160)
mitre: TA0001 Initial Access / T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application
actions: Patch OpenSSL on the target immediately.
Revoke and reissue TLS certificates/keys; force password resets.
Assume memory contents leaked: review what the server held.

incidents.title: Botnet / Command and Control
mitre: TA0011 Command and Control / T1071 Application Layer Protocol
actions: Isolate the internal host: it is likely already compromised.
Block the controller address/domain at the firewall and DNS.
Run endpoint forensics on the host and look for the same beacon elsewhere.

incidents.title: Port Scan / Reconnaissance
mitre: TA0043 Reconnaissance / T1595 Active Scanning
TA0007 Discovery / T1046 Network Service Discovery
actions: Block or tarpit the scanning source; check whether it is an internal host.
Review which ports answered and close services that should not be exposed.
Raise monitoring on the scanned hosts: an attack often follows a scan.

incidents.title: Web Application Attack
mitre: TA0001 Initial Access / T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application
actions: Inspect the web server / WAF logs for the payloads sent by the source.
Block the source and enable WAF rules for SQLi / XSS.
Check the application database for unexpected changes or data access.

incidents.title: Distributed Denial of Service
mitre: TA0040 Impact / T1498 Network Denial of Service
actions: Engage upstream DDoS scrubbing / CDN protection for the targeted address.
Apply geo or ASN rate limits; block the top offending source ranges.
Watch service health and bandwidth on the targeted link.

incidents.title: Network Infiltration
mitre: TA0002 Execution / T1204 User Execution
TA0008 Lateral Movement / T1021 Remote Services
actions: Isolate the internal host immediately and preserve it for forensics.
Find how the payload arrived (email, download) and block that path.
Hunt for the same behaviour on other hosts; reset credentials used on the host.

incidents.title: Port Scan / Reconnaissance
mitre: TA0043 Reconnaissance / T1595 Active Scanning
TA0007 Discovery / T1046 Network Service Discovery
actions: Block or tarpit the scanning source; check whether it is an internal host.
Review which ports answered and close services that should not be exposed.
Raise monitoring on the scanned hosts: an attack often follows a scan.

incidents.title: Denial of Service
mitre: TA0040 Impact / T1499 Endpoint Denial of Service
actions: Rate-limit or temporarily block the source at the edge firewall / load balancer.
Check the target service for exhausted worker pools or connection tables.
Enable slow-request timeouts (e.g. reverse-proxy header/body timeouts).

incidents.title: Network Infiltration
mitre: TA0002 Execution / T1204 User Execution
TA0008 Lateral Movement / T1021 Remote Services
actions: Isolate the internal host immediately and preserve it for forensics.
Find how the payload arrived (email, download) and block that path.
Hunt for the same behaviour on other hosts; reset credentials used on the host.

incidents.title: Credential Brute Force
mitre: TA0006 Credential Access / T1110 Brute Force
actions: Lock or throttle the targeted accounts; block the source IP.
Check authentication logs for any successful login from the source.
Enforce MFA and key-based SSH; disable password login where possible.

incidents.title: Botnet / Command and Control
mitre: TA0011 Command and Control / T1071 Application Layer Protocol
actions: Isolate the internal host: it is likely already compromised.
Block the controller address/domain at the firewall and DNS.
Run endpoint forensics on the host and look for the same beacon elsewhere.

incidents.title: Distributed Denial of Service
mitre: TA0040 Impact / T1498 Network Denial of Service
actions: Engage upstream DDoS scrubbing / CDN protection for the targeted address.
Apply geo or ASN rate limits; block the top offending source ranges.
Watch service health and bandwidth on the targeted link.

incidents.title: Web Application Attack
mitre: TA0001 Initial Access / T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application
actions: Inspect the web server / WAF logs for the payloads sent by the source.
Block the source and enable WAF rules for SQLi / XSS.
Check the application database for unexpected changes or data access.

insights: 3,794 alerts are novel (no known attack signature matched). Review them first for zero-day activity, then mark confirmed false positives so the baseline can learn them.
Unknown anomalous behaviour: one source touched 579 ports; treat it as reconnaissance and expect follow-up attacks on the open ones.
Port Scan / Reconnaissance: one source touched 955 ports; treat it as reconnaissance and expect follow-up attacks on the open ones.
Most alerts are low-confidence (only one model agrees). Consider a stricter alert budget (lower --fpr) if analysts are overloaded.

incidents.title: Port Scan / Reconnaissance
mitre: TA0043 Reconnaissance / T1595 Active Scanning
TA0007 Discovery / T1046 Network Service Discovery
actions: Block or tarpit the scanning source; check whether it is an internal host.
Review which ports answered and close services that should not be exposed.
Raise monitoring on the scanned hosts: an attack often follows a scan.

incidents.title: Botnet / Command and Control
mitre: TA0011 Command and Control / T1071 Application Layer Protocol
actions: Isolate the internal host: it is likely already compromised.
Block the controller address/domain at the firewall and DNS.
Run endpoint forensics on the host and look for the same beacon elsewhere.

incidents.title: Denial of Service
mitre: TA0040 Impact / T1499 Endpoint Denial of Service
actions: Rate-limit or temporarily block the source at the edge firewall / load balancer.
Check the target service for exhausted worker pools or connection tables.
Enable slow-request timeouts (e.g. reverse-proxy header/body timeouts).

incidents.title: Unknown anomalous behaviour
actions: Review the top deviating features listed in the explanation.
Check whether the source/destination is expected to talk this way.
If benign, mark it as a false positive so it can be learned as normal.

incidents.title: Web Application Attack
mitre: TA0001 Initial Access / T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application
actions: Inspect the web server / WAF logs for the payloads sent by the source.
Block the source and enable WAF rules for SQLi / XSS.
Check the application database for unexpected changes or data access.

incidents.title: Credential Brute Force
mitre: TA0006 Credential Access / T1110 Brute Force
actions: Lock or throttle the targeted accounts; block the source IP.
Check authentication logs for any successful login from the source.
Enforce MFA and key-based SSH; disable password login where possible.

incidents.title: Distributed Denial of Service
mitre: TA0040 Impact / T1498 Network Denial of Service
actions: Engage upstream DDoS scrubbing / CDN protection for the targeted address.
Apply geo or ASN rate limits; block the top offending source ranges.
Watch service health and bandwidth on the targeted link.
